subject: Finalizing MAP and SLA concessions for ACME pilot
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: priya@acme.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope + MAP draft

Rafael —

Thanks for the MAP draft. Priya and I reviewed it and we like the phased approach, but before we sign we need clarity on two commercial points that are blockers for our execs:

1) Pricing/discounts tied to ramp: We need a clear ramp schedule and the associated committed spend/discounts. Finance wants to know the breakpoints (pilot -> production) and what discounts apply at each step.

2) SLA/latency concessions: Our product team needs a firm latency SLO for the primary inference path. We understand there will be tradeoffs if you provide a discount — we need the precise SLOs, measurement windows, and remedies/credits if targets aren't met.

Can you produce a single-page summary that ties MAP milestones to pricing and the exact SLO language? If legal can give us a clean carve for scheduled maintenance and force majeure, that helps too.

Also copying a couple of questions inline from Priya: do you support per-route routing so we can fail over to an internal model if we breach SLOs? And what telemetry will you expose to our ops team?

Best,
Alex
VP, Product — ACME Corp

---
(Attachment referenced: internal_notes_from_acme.pdf)
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope + MAP draft

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a concise one-page commercial appendix that ties the MAP milestones to pricing, ramp commitments, and the SLA appendix we propose (see MutualActionPlan_v3.pdf and SLA-Appendix.docx). High level summary below and next steps:

Summary of proposed commercial linkage
- Pilot (8 weeks): No committed spend, PD (proof-of-data) credits applied; 10% onboarding discount on list rates for first 90 days.
- Ramp to limited production (month 3–6): 6‑month committed capacity @ 50k tokens/day average with a 15% committed discount. Commitment triggers 1x engineering onboarding and extended telemetry access.
- Production commit (month 7+): Annual commit option with 12‑month term; 20% discount at or above 200k tokens/day sustained.

SLA / latency SLOs tied to concessions
- Agreed production SLO (95th percentile gen latency): <= 150ms end-to-end for the primary inference path measured over 30 days.
- If 95p latency is between 150–200ms for two consecutive 30-day windows, commercial remedy: service credit of 5% of monthly committed fee for each window.
- If 95p latency >200ms for two consecutive windows, customer may request a 30-day remediation plan or terminate the committed portion without penalty.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (72-hour advance notice for rolling upgrades), force majeure, and customer-induced traffic spikes outside agreed ramp profile.

Telemetry and routing
- We will provide a telemetry feed (per-route p95/p99, error rates, token counts) accessible via a read-only dashboard and a streaming metrics endpoint to your ops team.
- Per-route routing and automatic fallback to either a smaller local model or our cheaper variant is supported; MAP will define which routes are eligible for fallback during SLO breaches.

Next steps
1) Legal: Priyom, can you please confirm the SLO language and credit calculation in SLA-Appendix.docx?
2) ACME: Alex/Priya, please review the attached 1-page commercial summary and confirm the ramp breakpoints (50k / 200k tokens/day).
3) If agreed, I’ll issue a term sheet and a DocuSign envelope for the committed portion.

I’m available for a 30-minute call this afternoon if that helps close these open points.

— Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0183
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope + MAP draft

Rafael / team —

Quick legal read below (attached SLA-Appendix.docx with tracked changes). Major items to confirm with ACME before signing:

1) Measurement window and metric source: We propose that p95 is measured from ingress at our API gateway to token emission completion, averaged daily and reported monthly. We need ACME to accept our gateway as the measurement point rather than their client-side timings.

2) Credit formula: Propose a capped credit of up to 15% of monthly committed fee per quarter. This prevents runaway credit exposure while giving ACME a meaningful remedy.

3) Exclusions and maintenance: Define a maintenance blackout of 4 hours/week for high-impact upgrades with 72-hour notice; extended maintenance requires calendar coordination.

4) Safety valve: If a sustained degradation is the result of ACME increasing traffic >25% above committed ramp without prior notice, we treat it as customer-induced and credit is void.

I added alternative wording for the termination clause tied to remediation timelines — see redlines. If we keep the termination right, restrict it to committed-cap portion only; we should preserve hosted API revenue for non-committed usage.

I’ll prep a clean term sheet and coordinate with finance on the credit cap math so we can present a final commercial appendix.

— Priyom Das
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SLA-Appendix.docx)
From: Alex Green <alex.green@acme.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: priya@acme.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope + MAP draft

Rafael / team —

Thanks — the one-pager is exactly what the exec committee needed. We reviewed Priyom's redlines and the credit cap looks OK from our side; we just need one change: replace the 30-day remediation window with a 45-day remediation window for production termination to give our SREs time to coordinate fallbacks.

Assuming you accept that tweak, we can sign the MAP and close the committed pilot by end of week. Please send the DocuSign envelope and the final pricing-summary.xlsx attached to the term sheet.

Alex
VP, Product — ACME Corp
